clue.text: Label promises unreliable

blocks.note: to dub is to give a name or label to
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: A record label's promises turn out not to be worth much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Label' looks like a noun but works as the verb dub; IOUS is the plural of IOU.
explanation.definitionFit: Something doubtful or questionable cannot be trusted, matching a source that is not dependable.

clue.text: Easily managed party on Channel Islands with the French

blocks.note: a do is an informal party
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands
le is the masculine form of the in French

explanation.surface: A party in Jersey or Guernsey, with French guests, goes off without trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands lie off the coast of Normandy and are British Crown dependencies.
explanation.definitionFit: A docile person or animal is compliant and submissive, so easy to control.

clue.text: Athletic support with navy borders

indicators.note: borders keeps only the outside edge letters of the word before it

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
W is an abbreviation for with
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A sports bra trimmed in navy blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Athletic support' suggests a sporting garment, but the definition is just the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Brawny describes someone strong and muscular, as an athletic build is.

clue.text: Hostility in work place

blocks.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
a place or spot is a position

explanation.surface: Antagonism among colleagues at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work place' reads as one word, workplace, but splits into two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposition is resistance or antagonism shown towards someone, which is hostility.

clue.text: Series of notes left in Chesterfield, perhaps

indicators.note: in puts the left abbreviation inside the furniture word

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
a chesterfield is a type of padded leather sofa; perhaps marks the example

explanation.surface: Sheet music abandoned in the town of Chesterfield.
explanation.walkthrough: Chesterfield is a Derbyshire town, but a chesterfield is also a deep-buttoned sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: Sol-fa is the system naming the scale do, re, mi and so on, a set of musical notes.

clue.text: Loses first of many independent butchers

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: opening letter of the word
standard abbreviation for independent
to butcher people is to slay them

explanation.surface: Many independent butcher's shops are going out of business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butchers' reads as a plural noun for shopkeepers but is a verb meaning kills.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislay something is to put it down somewhere forgotten, so you lose track of it.

clue.text: Mix-up by green cycling courier

indicators.note: cycling suggests the letters are spun around into a new order

blocks.note: a mix-up is a mess
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An eco-friendly bike courier causes a muddle in deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: A messenger carries messages or packages, which is what a courier does.

clue.text: Cats and dogs up for walk?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: cats and dogs are common household pets

explanation.surface: Is it raining cats and dogs, or are the animals keen for a walk?
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a single pace, and to step is to walk a short way.

clue.text: Disturbed American fool polished off by Democratic leader

indicators.note: leader picks out only the initial letter of the word before it

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
git is British slang for a stupid person
to polish off food is to eat it all
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A troubled American idiot is defeated by the leader of the Democrats.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitated means anxious and unsettled, which is what disturbed means of a person's mind.

clue.text: Add name to letters as way of giving direction

blocks.note: to sign is to put your name on something
letters delivered are the post

explanation.surface: Advice on signing correspondence as a means of instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way' here is a method, though it also hints at roads.
explanation.definitionFit: A signpost stands at a junction showing travellers which road leads where.

clue.text: Pain of male in very poor surroundings

indicators.note: in places the male sign inside the word for very poor

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
slang for something of very poor quality; surroundings marks it as the outer word

explanation.surface: A man suffers pain living in squalid conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: A cramp is a sudden painful contraction of a muscle, one specific kind of pain.

clue.text: Schedule final without daughter hearing

indicators.note: without says the final is taken minus the daughter abbreviation

blocks.note: a schedule is a list of items or times
the final part is the ending
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A timetable for a cup final that a daughter will miss, being heard in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final' is a noun for the end part here, not a sporting match.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing, as a participle, means paying attention to sounds, just as listening does.

clue.text: Places sand around pictures

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about and rearranged

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sprinkles sand around framed pictures, perhaps for a craft project.
explanation.definitionFit: Landscapes are paintings or photographs of countryside scenery, a type of picture.

clue.text: Complain of vehicle parking

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Drivers grumbling about where they can leave their cars.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to find fault and grumble persistently about trivial things.

clue.text: Appearance exactly two hours before Cinderella left ball

blocks.clueFragment: exactly two hours before Cinderella left
blocks.note: Cinderella fled the ball at midnight, so two hours earlier is at ten precisely
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Cinderella showed up at the ball and left on the dot, a fairy-tale timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The clock striking twelve is the fairy-tale detail that unlocks the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendance is the act of being present, and making an appearance means turning up.

clue.text: Allowing head of treasury a smaller amount is inconsiderate

indicators.note: head of takes just the leading letter of the next word

blocks.note: allowing in the sense of granting that, as a conjunction
opening letter of the word
less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: Giving the Treasury chief a reduced budget is deemed unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Allowing' looks like permitting, but here it means granting that, a sense shared with though.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoughtless person fails to consider other people's feelings, which is being inconsiderate.

clue.text: Stubborn botanist repositioned bottom of vine

indicators.note: repositioned says these letters are moved into new places
in a down clue, bottom of means the final letter of the word

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A determined plant scientist moves the lower end of a grapevine.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate and stubborn both describe someone who refuses to change their mind.

clue.text: Stress caused by ecstasy and speed unaltered

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
miles per hour, a unit of speed
as is means left unchanged

explanation.surface: Anxiety brought on by taking party drugs, ecstasy and speed.
explanation.walkthrough: Speed sounds like a second drug, but it gives the unit of velocity.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is the stress placed on a word or idea to give it importance.

clue.text: Alienate English eccentric

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
an eccentric person is odd or strange

explanation.surface: An oddball Englishman who puts people off.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to make someone hostile or distant, the same as alienating them.

clue.text: Military Intelligence's prisoners right to grasp wrong end of stick

blocks.note: MI is Military Intelligence, plus the possessive S
cons, short for convicts, are prisoners
true as in correct or right

explanation.surface: Intelligence officers' captives are within their rights to misunderstand what is happening.
explanation.definitionFit: To misconstrue is to interpret wrongly, the same as misunderstanding the situation entirely.

clue.text: German traitor lives free

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for German
a rat is a betrayer or informer
is in the sense of exists or lives

explanation.surface: A German turncoat is living without paying rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like free from prison, but it means costing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis means without charge, so something given gratis costs nothing at all.

clue.text: A little-known connection?

blocks.note: surface reading: an obscure link between people or ideas
setter's reading: the short punctuation mark joining little and known in the clue itself

explanation.walkthrough: The clue demonstrates its own answer: the dash in 'little-known' is the connection.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyphen is the short punctuation mark that links two words into a compound term.

clue.text: Difficult to remove top from UK's tallest building

indicators.note: remove top means the opening letter of the building's name is dropped

blocks.note: the Shard in London is the tallest building in the UK

explanation.surface: Taking the top off Britain's tallest skyscraper would be a tough job.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shard is a 310-metre glass tower by London Bridge; behead it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard and difficult are synonyms for something requiring great effort.

clue.text: Treat with contempt hospital attendant that's unruly

blocks.note: to dis someone is to disrespect them
an orderly is an attendant in a hospital

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a hospital porter who misbehaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorderly behaviour is wild and out of control, just like unruly conduct.

clue.text: Part of cricket game broadcast finally to public

indicators.note: finally keeps just the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Cricket coverage finally being shown on public television.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly and not hidden, so it is public in the sense of visible.

clue.text: Food plan doesn't include eating tofu initially

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of each of the preceding words

blocks.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A meal plan that leaves out tofu, perhaps for a confirmed meat-eater.
explanation.walkthrough: The four words before 'initially' give one letter each.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a planned regime of what you eat, so a plan for food.

clue.text: Iced nasty criminal group

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent out of their order

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Gangland slang: a nasty mob has iced, or killed, someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal group' looks like the whole definition, but criminal is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndicate is an association of people or firms combining for a shared business purpose.

clue.text: Nick is not going to Switzerland

blocks.note: taken as written
CH is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: A man called Nick is cancelling a Swiss trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name but is a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick and a notch are both small V-shaped cuts made in an edge or surface.

clue.text: Respect lively spirit

indicators.note: lively suggests the letters jump around into a new order

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to honour a vivacious personality.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is a ghost, and spirit can mean a ghostly apparition too.

clue.text: Time to debate disloyalty

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to reason is to argue a matter out

explanation.surface: A call to parliament to discuss betrayal of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betraying one's country or sovereign, the gravest form of faithlessness.
